resources.string: Brown Diatom
Soft brown film or dust on glass, plants and hardscape, especially in newer aquariums.
Green Spot Algae
Hard green dots on glass and older, slow-growing leaves.
Green Dust Algae
Soft green dust-like film that wipes off glass easily and can settle again quickly.
Green Algae Coat
Broader green patina on glass, rocks, wood or equipment that is not clearly spot or dust algae.
Black Beard Algae
Short, dark brush-like tufts attached firmly to leaves, wood, rocks and equipment.
Staghorn Algae
Grey-green branching strands that resemble small antlers.
Fuzz Algae
Very short individual green filaments, often on plant leaves and decoration.
Hair Algae
Longer soft green strands forming tangled or carpet-like growth on plants and hardscape.
Thread / String Algae
Fine, long individual green threads that hang from plants or become caught on decoration.
Fluff Algae
Very soft, light-green cottony cushions or fluffy tufts.
Cladophora
Coarse, tough branching green tufts that resist breaking and cling to plants or hardscape.
Blue-Green Slime
Slimy blue-green sheets; technically cyanobacteria rather than algae.
Green Water
Free-floating microscopic algae that turn the water cloudy green.
